story.title: Troy Jackson Secures Senate Seat in Maine, Defeating Susan Collins
story.summary: Democrat Troy Jackson has won the U.S. Senate race in Maine, defeating incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins. Jackson, a former state Senate president and logger, became the Democratic nominee after Graham Platner withdrew from the race in July. His victory is seen as a significant gain for the Democratic Party in the midterm elections.

explore_lenses.label: What changed in Maine’s Senate representation?
explore_lenses.title: A longtime Republican seat is projected to flip
explore_lenses.summary: Jackson’s projected win would end Susan Collins’s nearly 30-year Senate tenure and give Maine a Democratic U.S. senator for the first time since 1995.

claims.text: The Associated Press called the race for Democrat Troy Jackson; Collins conceded before the AP call, according to contemporaneous reporting.
Jackson’s win would end Collins’s service after almost 30 years in Congress; she was first elected to the Senate in 1996.
Jackson would be Maine’s first Democratic U.S. senator since 1995.

explore_lenses.label: What arguments defined the Jackson-Collins contest?
explore_lenses.title: Affordability and independence were competing themes
explore_lenses.summary: Jackson presented Collins as too aligned with Republican national policy, while Collins emphasized her Senate influence and record of delivering for Maine.

claims.text: Jackson argued that Collins had not opposed President Trump strongly enough and highlighted her vote for Justice Brett Kavanaugh, which he linked to the Supreme Court’s 2022 abortion-rights decision.
Collins argued that her seniority and influence in the Senate had benefited Maine; she also questioned Jackson’s legislative effectiveness.

Jackson emphasized his background as a logger and labor advocate and ran on making life more affordable, while Democratic consultant Toby McGrath characterized his appeal as rooted in working-class advocacy.

explore_lenses.label: When would Jackson formally take the Senate seat?
explore_lenses.title: Certification comes before the January term begins
explore_lenses.summary: Maine still must complete its statutory canvass and issue an election certificate. If the result is certified and Jackson is seated, the new six-year Senate term begins January 3, 2027.

claims.text: Maine’s Secretary of State must tabulate returns and submit a certified copy to the governor within 20 days after the election; the tabulation is final on submission except where a recount is pending.
Maine law provides that the Secretary of State prepares, and the governor signs, an election certificate for each person elected under the state tabulation.
The Maine secretary of state described the November 4 UOCAVA figures as unofficial; in that separate overseas and uniformed-service tally, Jackson received 4,350 votes and Collins received 473.
Senate terms last six years, and the incumbent Class II term ends January 3, 2027; the Constitution requires members of Congress to be bound by oath or affirmation.

story_report.summary: Democrat Troy Jackson has been declared the winner of Maine’s U.S. Senate race over Republican incumbent Susan Collins, after the Associated Press called the contest and Collins conceded. Jackson, who became the Democratic nominee after Graham Platner withdrew in July, is poised to end Collins’s nearly 30-year congressional career. If the result is certified, Jackson would become Maine’s first Democratic U.S. senator since 1995.

sections.heading: Campaign Arguments Framed the Contest
sections.body: Jackson argued that Collins had not opposed President Donald Trump strongly enough and criticized her vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh, linking it to the Supreme Court’s 2022 abortion-rights decision. Collins campaigned on her Senate seniority and influence on Maine’s behalf, while questioning Jackson’s legislative effectiveness. Jackson emphasized his experience as a logger and labor advocate and ran on affordability.

sections.heading: Maine Certification Process Remains
sections.body: The race call and concession do not substitute for Maine’s official statewide certification. State law requires the secretary of state to tabulate returns and submit a certified copy to the governor within 20 days of the election; the governor then signs election certificates prepared by the secretary of state. The incumbent Class II Senate term ends Jan. 3, 2027, and Senate terms run for six years.

unresolved.text: As of Nov. 4, 2026, official statewide results, any recount request and final certification had not been identified in the Maine results portal consulted.

related_stories.title: Democrats Gain Control of Congress in Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: In a significant shift during the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats have regained control of both the House and Senate, marking their first full control of Congress since 2023. This outcome allows them to block President Trump's nominees and influence his agenda. The election results reflect a broader dissatisfaction with Trump's leadership, particularly in light of ongoing issues such as the Iran war.
